reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is extracting actionable patterns from high-dimensional spatio-temporal player trajectories. Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Clustering maps raw GPS data onto latent clusters representing typical movement signatures. It leverages k-means or DBSCAN under the assumption of local spatial coherence, but fails catastrophically when players move in non-Euclidean manifolds (e.g., curved court geometry). Motion Chart Visualization extends this by animating cluster assignments over time, projecting four dimensions (x,y,t,cluster ID) onto a 2D screen using size (player importance) and color (action type). This provides a holistic view of coordinated motion but suffers from overplotting at scale. Finally, Spacing Structure Analysis quantifies the geometric regularity within these clusters, measuring pairwise distances to infer spacing optimality. Together, they form a dual-layer filter: the first extracts coherent motion manifolds, while the second evaluates whether those manifolds align with strategic objectives (e.g., wide spacing for perimeter shooters). Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring that clustering features are decorrelated (e.g., velocity vs. direction).
